steps.name: Calm Voice
steps.text: She hasn't come to?

steps.name: Nervous Voice
steps.text: Not yet, doc. The whole tribe has been waiting here all afternoon.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Hnngh...

steps.name: Calm Voice
steps.text: Is anyone in a rush to see the doctor?

steps.name: Nervous Voice
steps.text: No, we're in no rush. You should save the girl first! She's cursed!

steps.name: Calm Voice
steps.text: She came from the waterfall?

steps.name: Nervous Voice
steps.text: Yeah, that's right. I checked her front and back. She's got no rocks, and she's not hurt. She's holding a tablet she won't let go, though.

steps.name: Nervous Voice
steps.text: She was muttering some strange sounds in the morning, but then she quieted down.

steps.name: Nervous Voice
steps.text: And when I checked on her just now, it was like her breathing had stopped!

steps.name: No Longer Calm Voice
steps.text: —Huh?! Why didn't you say that right away?

steps.name: Nervous Voice
steps.text: If you can't save the girl, then at least help us break her curse. This is my home...

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: Hey, girl, can you hear me?

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: So... heavy... ugh...

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: Who put a heavy tablet like this on her chest?

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: Okay, I got that off you now.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Phew!

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: Good, you're responding. How do you feel?

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: I want some... mint Zubayr ice cream...

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: You sure you're all better?

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Yes, doctor. I don't have any professional medical knowledge, but... I'm well-practiced at collapsing due to heat stroke...

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: *sigh* Young lady, most people don't get heat strokes in this weather. Are you ill?

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: I'm fine, physically, but I have a few questions I'd like to ask you.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Please take a look at this leaf. Is this the Beastbrain Leaf mentioned in the book that's supposed to have a cool scent and mind-refreshing properties?

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: Throw that away right now.

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: I don't know this Beastbrain Leaf that you speak of, but I assure you that if you grind that leaf and apply it to your forehead, you will attract acid Originium slugs!

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Uh, okay... Th-Then, what about this fruit? Can I use it as an emergency ration for the road?

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: Eat that, and you will only get a taste of the afterlife.

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: What are you doing? Is that a notebook?

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Right, this is my Tentative Travel Plan (Final Draft). It means I'm fully prepared and have made up my mind... but... I suppose now it's (Final Draft-Revised)

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Thank you very much for your advice. Do you still have any more outdoor survival tips?

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: Just go home. There's no sightseeing to be done around here.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Yes, I understand.

steps.name: Impetuous Villager
steps.text: You are sure she's all better?

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: That's what she says.

steps.name: Impetuous Villager
steps.text: I don't think so. I still think she's cursed.

steps.name: Impetuous Villager
steps.text: My sister and I found her by the water this morning. She was completely out. Must've gone into the woods we're not supposed to go into.

steps.name: Impetuous Villager
steps.text: She kept murmuring the whole time, and she was really loud, too. Even louder than how she's talking now.

steps.name: Gentle Villager
steps.text: Yes, she kept saying she was looking for some totem, some cans with guts in them... She even started ordering people around.

steps.name: Impetuous Villager
steps.text: Exactly, I remember too! She kept muttering this one's been dead for so long and that one's been buried for years. What normal person says that?!

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Impetuous Villager
steps.text: If she does anything weird again, I'll cut down all the bad things, just like we cut trees!

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: Relax, you two. Feeble as she is, she couldn't do anything to hurt anyone, or even get too far on her own.

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: Alright, who else needs attending to—

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: H-Help!

steps.name: Gentle Villager
steps.text: Dear me, why are there so many slugs?!

steps.name: Impetuous Villager
steps.text: C-C-Ca-Calm down! We're coming to help!

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: I'm sorry...

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: Didn't I warn you that the plant attracts Originium slugs literally a minute ago?!

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: I tripped on my way out of the village...

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: ...then I bumped my head into the tree and spooked the slugs under the branches. I got down on the ground and used Arts to try and protect myself, but I didn't get my aim right...

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: Don't push yourself like that.

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: The lords ameer used to send people like you here. They'd search the wilds and take home rocks as prizes.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: What happened after that? Did they leave empty-handed?

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: How would I know? They came and went, yet life here has remained the same. The little holes they dug were instantly filled up in a single rising tide.

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: If you really think you could find any kind of 'history' in this place...

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: It's okay. I'm not afraid of disappointment.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: I've made up my mind this time. Now that I've actually left home, I have to see everything here with my own eyes.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: I can decipher the text on this tablet, so I'll investigate everything based on the information written here... even if it doesn't lead to any worthwhile discoveries.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: —Besides, I've gathered over a hundred 'Spectacular Rainforest Tribes Sights' from my books. The forest is huge, but I should be able to see at least one, right?

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: *sigh*. Here, take these herbs. Heat stroke treatment, insect repellent, anti-emetic, even wild beast repellent... Just about everything you'll need.

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: I'll be heading to another village soon. The Archosauria here are kind, but they may not be able to understand you, much less help you.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Okay, thank you...

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Right, doctor, may I ask you one more question? The villagers mentioned some kind of curse. Do you know what that is?

steps.name: Enthusiastic Villager
steps.text: Right, like this. Tie a knot around yourself with the vines, then swing it to the other side.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Villager
steps.text: You have to use one hand to hold the vines, though, so set down that big stone you're holding.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: It's okay. I can hold it under my arm.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Also, this is not a normal stone. It's inscribed with words.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: I've been collecting tablets like this one for some time now. If you find any like it, please do bring them to me. I can pay you for them.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Villager
steps.text: Stones with words on them? I've heard about them.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Really? From whom? May I talk to them?

steps.name: Enthusiastic Villager
steps.text: Well, he's been lying under the ground for a while now. That's what you get for going to the cursed forest. We don't even know if he's worth pitying.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: I figured. All the tablets that could be monuments are placed right at the edge of that forest...

steps.name: Enthusiastic Villager
steps.text: What were you saying?

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: N-Nothing. I'm asking if you could help swing me over to the shore on the other side.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Villager
steps.text: No problem! One, two, let's go—

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Wraaaaaaggghhhh—

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Hold on! My tablet! I'm going to drop it—

steps.name: Enthusiastic Villager
steps.text: Don't let go! Don't grab—

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: H-Help—ugh...

steps.name: Gentle Villager
steps.text: Papyrus, you're back! You were gone for so long, I thought you'd left—

steps.name: Gentle Villager
steps.text: Dear me, why are you all drenched again? Had another fall in the water?

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: N-No... It was the rain... Achoo!

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Izaja, register this tablet... Right, the weather forecast tablet that other tribe gave me. Not that knowing it'd rain would help me at all...

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Mm... Izaja... Why are you just standing there, not working?

steps.name: Gentle Villager
steps.text: W-Who are you talking to?

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: —Oh no, you're not Izaja!

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Sorry, please forget whatever I just said...! There's no other tribe! I-I was just... Ah...

steps.name: Gentle Villager
steps.text: —You're burning up. No wonder you're talking nonsense.

steps.name: Gentle Villager
steps.text: *sigh*... No more talk of curses. Poor thing. Let's head back inside and get some rest.

steps.name: Gentle Villager
steps.text: Once you're feeling better, I'll tell you which tree oil you can put on your clothes to waterproof them and keep Originium slugs from climbing up your legs.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Thanks...

steps.name: Gentle Villager
steps.text: Silly girl, I don't understand why you keep thanking people. I didn't put the trees there, I'm just telling you how to use them.

steps.name: Gentle Villager
steps.text: After I tell you, you can go tell the next person who could use the knowledge.

steps.name: Gentle Villager
steps.text: Alright, let's go.

steps.name: Stout Villager
steps.text: Papyrus, why are trying to chop a tree? You need strength for work like this. Can I help?

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: *gasp*... *gasp*... No thanks... I'm fine...

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: I just wanted to see if this Arts-powered chainsaw could really save some strength...

steps.name: Stout Villager
steps.text: That looks amazing! Can I try?

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Of course! Just let me figure out how to turn it off first...

steps.name: Stout Villager
steps.text: Uh, hold on. Papyrus? Don't make that thing spin so fast! You're facing it the wrong way!

steps.name: Stout Villager
steps.text: Out of the way!

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: S-Sorry...!

steps.name: Stout Villager
steps.text: Haha! I knew it! Every time you head out, you bring back some really useful toys!

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: R-Right... Anyway, I'll make sure your roof gets fixed...

steps.name: Impetuous Villager
steps.text: Whoa, this is good!

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Hold on... That tablet isn't for frying fowlbeast eggs...

steps.name: Impetuous Villager
steps.text: You just want to look at the drawings, right? I'll clean it up before giving it back.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Okay...

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Are you not worried about the curse anymore?

steps.name: Impetuous Villager
steps.text: What's there to worry about? You've got plenty of those tablets and you're still fine. I even checked on my grandma's grave—if she hasn't crawled back out, then it means nothing bad has happened.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Has she... crawled out before?

steps.name: Impetuous Villager
steps.text: Never, haha! You know, I'm a really lucky guy.

steps.name: Impetuous Villager
steps.text: Eh, that reminds me, Papyrus. How come I haven't ever heard you tell any stories about yourself?

steps.name: Impetuous Villager
steps.text: I told you about the tree that made the spear I used to kill my first prey, but you haven't shared where you come from, how big your tribe is, or how many fistfights you've won...

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: I... I don't have anything interesting to talk about.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: I didn't spend much time with people my age, and I rarely had a chance to step outside my family's manor. All I had in my life was books.

steps.name: Impetuous Villager
steps.text: Oh, books! What books do the traders there sell? I love the ones that are all pictures!

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: No, I'm afraid it's not quite what you're thinking...

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: I come from a family of academics, so we have a large collection of treasured literature at home that is maintained and expanded by each generation.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Of course, we have books on a variety of topics, but like many people in our city, my father thinks history is the most noble of knowledge.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: As for myself... I'm not sure if I like it or just got used to it because I had no other choice. I might be more familiar with how people lived two thousand years ago than my own life.

steps.name: Impetuous Villager
steps.text: Two thousand? Whoa, that's like my grandmother's grandmother's grandmother's...

steps.name: Impetuous Villager
steps.text: I don't even know how far back it goes! It sounds like you know lots of really fun things, Papyrus!

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Fun things...? Right, there used to be a small number of scholars who speculated that the Manticores were the lords of the rainforest, idols worshiped by all.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: They pointed to a skeleton found in a massive tomb as evidence, but later, more advanced technology proved that they were simply too creative when they put the skeleton back together.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: They put the bones back together in the wrong spots, and made an Archosauria look like a Manticore.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Speaking of Archosauria, there's also an especially famous 'entertainment hypothesis'.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: The reason that the Archosauria did not leave any traces in early recorded history is that their intelligence and technology had already developed to a level that was far beyond modern Sargon's.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: They had already more than satisfied their curiosity, and so they didn't want any contact with the outside world and intentionally erased all traces of any explorers who found them.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: And also...

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: ...Oh, I'm sorry! Once I get into my area of expertise, I tend to go on and on, even if I'm just having a laugh.

steps.name: Gentle Villager
steps.text: What's there to be sorry about? You were telling us a bunch of things we didn't know. It's fun.

steps.name: Stout Villager
steps.text: Right, every time I hear you say those strange words, it just pulls me in, like I'm possessed!

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Ahem... Okay, that was all just academic anecdotes. Whether you understand them or not, please don't take them seriously...

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: But there's really not much more I can tell besides the stories in my books.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Before I made up my mind to leave home and go on a journey, I had left Menat-Ha'mait, where I was born and raised, only once.

steps.name: Impetuous Villager
steps.text: Keep going!

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Okay... One day, I had an argument with a friend over some documents. She suddenly slammed on the desk, and said she was taking me to a mutual friend to reason things out.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Maybe we were both too agitated, but we didn't even think of trying the professors at the academy... She contacted a caravan, and we left with them.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: At first, I was really scared that my father would find out and punish me for wasting time and putting myself in danger.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: But actually, we ended up staying in a carriage compartment that was made to be like a bedroom. I kept following my routine and woke up at seven in the morning to keep working on my thesis.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Our mutual friend rushed to the closest town to meet up with us as well.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: The only things I remember about our meeting are her taking some scary photos of a tomb excavation site from unexpected angles for me...

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: And the weather being so terrible that I kept the window shut the entire trip.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: I know that was the right decision for my health, but I still wonder what it looked like outside the window.
The tribespeople all stare at each other, apparently not expecting the story to end so abruptly.
After a brief moment, right after somebody slurps a fowlbeast egg, one of the audience members breaks the silence.

steps.name: Impetuous Villager
steps.text: I've got a question. What's a compartment? How did it bring your whole room with you?

steps.name: Gentle Villager
steps.text: That reminds me, I also wanted to ask, what's an academy?
Papyrus finds herself surrounded by the Archosauria and bombarded with questions.
Some are ones that she had anticipated, while others are questions that she had never thought about.
From the library of her childhood home to the magnificent Varjavandabad Museum and then the Rhodes Island landship...
As she answers the questions, her boring life slowly sounds more vivid and colorful.
Finally, everyone asks her about her current trip.

steps.name: Impetuous Villager
steps.text: I still have one more question, Papyrus. You keep on bringing all those strange trinkets, like saws and stones that tell when it'll rain... Where did you get them?

steps.name: Enthusiastic Voice
steps.text: Louder! We're here to make friends! We need to be passionate, and more passionate than the other side!

steps.name: Enthusiastic Voice
steps.text: We'll shout the slogan Papyrus taught us! Nothing will go wrong!

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: 'Make friends', eh? Young lady, the villagers outside are mobilizing to enter the forbidden zone. That was all your idea, wasn't it?

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: I thought you'd have left by now.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: If I hadn't gotten sick or collapsed from exhaustion so much, I definitely would've left...

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: I'm sorry about the disagreement we had, doctor.

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: Looks like you didn't heed my advice.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: I just think that if the curse doesn't exist, then the other side of the rainforest they're so afraid of is just another tribe. They shouldn't be trapped by their ancestors' legends.

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: You insist on revealing the 'true history', even if it means hurting the ones who are alive.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: No... I've thought it over. Please let me explain.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Just as you said, I can't be sure what will happen when the two tribes make contact. There has been much bloodshed between tribes throughout history.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: That's why I've been going between the two tribes in order to compare and contrast them.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: If they once had a close relationship and still share common rituals, then the two sides would already have the foundation of a friendly encounter.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Uh, but actually... it was the inventions of the other tribes I've been bringing back that piqued their curiosity. Both sides proactively asked to meet their friends on the other side of the forest.

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: So this was not your idea.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Right. Thinking back, perhaps I was just playing the role of a Messenger.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Oh, doctor, they're planning to build a bridge by the waterfall. Maybe you won't have to take a detour through the foggiest part of the rainforest the next time you leave.

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: What about you?

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: You're a strange young lady. You could've come to this place in those air-conditioned metal monsters like those heralds of the lords ameer.

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: I can tell your social standing is even higher than theirs. You could've had someone dig up the history between these two tribes for you.

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: It is within your power to interfere in their lives by sending a Messenger to demand the two tribes form ties or even merge into one. I've seen that happen many times.

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: Why put yourself through all this trouble?

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Because I didn't want to come here for sightseeing... I want to know what it looks like outside the window.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Before I left home, someone I really respected once told me to discover the meaning of my journey for myself, and that I should never forget it, but also not think too highly of it.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: That's why I tried my hardest. Although going by the results, I guess the only thing that I've gained so far is a whole lot of nightmares...

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: But I think it's much better to have nightmares every time I see Originium slugs than to touch them curiously in the office before heading back to the desk to document with joy.

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: You really are a weird one.

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: Are you happy, after suffering through all that?

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Truth is... I do miss the air conditioning and purified water back in the office, and all the books and resources readily available.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Every day, I feel just how insignificant each one of my steps is compared to Sargon's long history.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: My father is right in that regard. Compared to my research, the weeks I've spent in this rainforest are all a waste of time.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: I was only able to persevere and stay here for such a long time because I wanted to finish one thing.

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: Those tablets.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Right.

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: You taught the locals a slogan. Looks like you got plenty of information out of those tablets.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Actually... those tablets only talk about their exploits and feats in battle.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Just as you predicted, the Archosauria are born combative. In the past, the two tribes often came to blows whenever they saw each other.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: I think... it's because somebody would go missing every time they went to the other side that the tribes slowly got the idea that the forest curses people.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: But I suppose the truth of the past doesn't really matter to the people alive right now, does it?

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: Very well... I'll keep that secret for you, and I'll keep an eye on the tribes so they don't come to blows again after you leave.

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: We'll call it my thanks to you for getting them to build this bridge and saving me some time in the future.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Thank you so much... Uh, if you wouldn't mind bringing me with you when you left this time, that'd be even better.

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: I want to make it to the closest town in one piece and enjoy an ice-cold glass of fruit juice before contacting the Rhodes Island office... I'll pay!

steps.name: Roaming Doctor
steps.text: Not standing by your principles anymore?

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Th-That's because I'm leaving!

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: Besides, now that the tribesmen are finally uniting and heading into the forest that they were so afraid of, in hopes of making new friends, I've finally realized...

steps.name: Papyrus
steps.text: In the end, the most important thing is taking that very first step.
